items.q: What is a couple's birth chart?
items.r: A birth chart is a map of the sky at the moment someone was born: where the Sun, the Moon and the planets were, seen from Earth. A couple's birth chart compares two of these maps. In astrology, this is called synastry.

items.q: Do we need to know our time of birth?
items.r: No. Without the time, we calculate everything at noon. That changes nothing for the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Mars, except on the rare days when one of them changes sign. The Moon, though, changes sign every two and a half days: if it changed sign on the day you were born, the report gives you both options.

items.q: How do I get the report?
items.r: It appears right after payment, on this page. We also send you its link by email, so you can find it again whenever you want.

items.q: Can I give it as a gift?
items.r: Yes! You just need both birth dates. The report link can be shared, and it opens on any phone.
No. No study has shown that the stars decide whether a relationship works. Read the report as a game for two: it gives you something to talk about, yourselves, what you want and how you differ.
Your first names and birth dates are only used to calculate your report. We keep them for six months after payment, then everything is deleted.

intros.carte: Here is the sky at the moment you were born, brought together on a single wheel. {{a}}'s planets are in pink on the outer ring, {{b}}'s in purple on the inside. In the middle, lines connect the planets that talk to each other: gold when they get along, dotted when they rub.
intros.profil: In astrology, two things count in a couple: harmony, everything that fits easily between your charts, and spark, everything that attracts and stirs. Your relationship sits somewhere between the two.
intros.domaines: Six big areas of life together, scored out of 100 from the links between your planets. A low score doesn't mean things are going badly: it's just where your charts understand each other least on their own.
intros.atouts: The most striking links between your two charts: the ones that carry you, and the ones that need a little attention.
intros.elements: Each sign belongs to an element: fire, earth, air or water. Here is where your ten planets fall, five each.
intros.chinois: Chinese astrology doesn't look at the planets, it looks at the year of birth: an animal and an element, which come back every sixty years.
intros.vie: In numerology, the life path is the sum of the digits of the birth date, reduced to a single digit. 11, 22 and 33 stay whole.
intros.annee: The twelve months ahead, based on where Venus, Mars and Jupiter move, and the periods when Mercury, Venus and Mars go backward in the sky.
intros.questions: Pick one tonight, and ask the other. The best conversations often start like that.

placements.doute: Without the time of birth, a planet that changes sign that day may be in one or the other. The report gives you both.

rapport.aucunAtout: No very gentle link between your charts: your bond is built day by day, more than it falls from the sky.
rapport.aucunDefi: No really tense link between your charts. Your challenges will be those of every couple!
